newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: New TV giant CLT-UFA aims to be Europe number one.
newsitem.headline: New TV giant CLT-UFA aims to be Europe number one.

text.p: Newly-created private television group CLT-UFA, whose partners already have strong market share, is aiming to become Europe's top broadcaster, co-chief executive officer Rolf Schmidt-Holtz on Tuesday.
"Our target is to become the number one television and radio group in Europe," he told a news conference presenting the group, the product of a merger between Luxembourg's CLT and Germany's UFA.
"In those markets where we are not already the leader, we want to become it," said Remy Sautter, its other CEO. "We plan to invest several hundreds of millions of marks per year."
Shareholders of CLT, a unit of Belgian-Luxembourg media holding company Audiofina, gave the final go-ahead on Monday for the merger with UFA, the television unit of German media concern Bertelsmann.
Bertelsmann and Audiofina signed an agreement to merge their audiovisual units in July last year but the deal has taken months to gain board and shareholder approval.
"CLT-UFA is the culmination of our television and radio strategy at Bertelsmann to become a truly international broadcasting company," Bertelsmann's Michael Dornemann said.
CLT-UFA leads the television market in Germany, the Netherlands and the French-speaking part of Belgium.
It is also market leader in French radio, has a strong position in French television, and has started operations in several other European countries, including Britain and Poland.
At the end of 1996 CLT-UFA had stakes in 19 TV and 23 radio stations in Europe, including RTL Television, which is market leader in Germany with an 18.2 percent audience share.
Sautter is in charge of television in non-German speaking countries and of radio. Schmidt-Holtz is head of television in German-speaking countries and of international rights.
Sautter said CLT-UFA wanted to expand in other northern and central European countries but declined to say where. "This will depend on the opportunities which come up," he said.
The group wants to develop pay television to complement free television, build a Europe-wide major position in production and rights acquisition and expand in radio.

Sautter expected the group would have 1997 turnover of about 100 billion Luxembourg francs ($3 billion). "Once we are at cruising speed, I hope we will have a net profit margin of five percent on turnover," he said.
Audiofina director Didier Bellens said that once the group was fully operational, the margin should be much higher.

The two CEOs said they had no regrets about dropping their ambitious plans for digital pay television in Germany late last year and played down any rivalries with Canal Plus, the French market leader in pay TV.

CLT-UFA remains active in pay television via minority stakes in German channel Premiere and French group TPS. Premiere had 1.4 million subscribers at the end of 1996 and TPS 13,000. ($1=32.75 Luxembourg Franc)
